tower.company.doc.rejected: Rejected, and kept with the reason.
tower.changes.title: What changed, and who changed it
tower.changes.hint: Newest first. A rate somebody set is a decision somebody made.
tower.changes.foldCount: {n, plural, one {# change} other {# changes}}, the last on {when}
tower.custodyCaps.title: Custody cap for the new
tower.custodyCaps.hint: How many parcels a new shop holds, and a new rider in no fleet carries, at once. Each limit grows by one with every parcel handed on and lifts after the number you set. Leave both boxes empty for no cap. A fleet’s drivers are not capped here: their fleet answers for them. Start low — a rider at 3, lifted after 50 — and raise it as your country learns who delivers.
tower.custodyCaps.effect: A shop at its limit takes nothing more in; a rider at theirs takes nothing more on. Both are told the limit and how it grows.
tower.custodyCaps.bad: Whole numbers, a start of at least 1, and lifted no sooner than it starts — or both boxes empty for no cap.
tower.custodyCaps.saved: Saved — the custody cap applies from now on
tower.sealRules.title: Seals
tower.sealRules.hint: Where this company requires a seal on loads taken over in its country. The shipper writes it before pickup and the driver reads it off the door; a required seal not written and the load is not taken over. The shipper and the driver are told it is this company’s rule.
tower.sealRules.question: Require a seal on
tower.sealRules.effectOn: A load you picked is not taken over until its shipper has written a seal.
tower.sealRules.effectOff: No seal is required. A shipper may still seal any load.
tower.sealRules.saved: Saved — a seal is now required where you said
tower.carrierPapers.title: Carrier papers
tower.carrierPapers.hint: A fleet’s transport licence and its goods-in-transit cover are recorded and shown on the Papers screen whatever you choose here. This decides only what a lapse DOES: enforced, the fleet’s runs come off the board and it can be sold no new work until the paper is renewed; not enforced, it stays a warning somebody has to act on. Runs already under way are always finished. Most fleets were onboarded without these dates — record them before you enforce, or nothing will change.
tower.carrierPapers.question: Stop selling a carrier’s space when this has lapsed
tower.carrierPapers.effectOn: A lapsed paper you picked takes that carrier off the board. A paper with no date recorded never does.
tower.carrierPapers.effectOff: Nothing is enforced. Lapses are shown on the Papers screen and cost nobody work.
tower.carrierPapers.saved: Saved — lapsed carrier papers now take a fleet off the board
tower.carrierPapers.savedNone: Saved — no carrier papers are enforced
tower.carrierPapers.listHint: Each fleet’s own transport licence and cover. Shown whether or not the company behind it enforces them — a paper nobody looks at is how this licence went unchecked.
tower.carrierPapers.none: No fleet has finished onboarding yet.
tower.carrierPapers.enforcedNone: Nothing — a lapse is a warning only
tower.carrierPapers.refusedDone: Turned down — the fleet sees your reason on its dashboard
tower.carrierPapers.sentRowOne: A document sent {date} — waiting on us
tower.carrierPapers.sentRowMany: Both documents sent, the latest {date} — waiting on us
tower.carrierPapers.sentRead: Sent {date}. They read the expiry as {expires}.
tower.carrierPapers.sentNumber: Number on it, as they read it: {number}.
tower.carrierPapers.readDate: Expiry date, as YOU read it on the document
tower.carrierPapers.differs: That is not the date they read ({expires}). Look at the document again before recording it.
tower.carrierPapers.refuseWhy: Why — the fleet office reads this sentence as you write it
tower.courierCover.title: Their insurance cover
tower.courierCover.sentRead: Sent {date}. They read it as running until {expires}; policy {policy}.
tower.courierCover.differs: They read {expires}. Two readings of one policy that disagree are worth a second look.
tower.courierCover.hint: Read off the policy they sent. While it runs, loads whose sender asks for cover are open to them, and their notes name the cover.
tower.courierCover.why: Why it is not accepted (they are shown this)
tower.courierCover.onRecord: Cover on record until {expires}, policy {policy} — read by {who}, {date}.
tower.courierCover.refusedLast: The last policy they sent was refused: “{reason}”.
tower.courierCover.recordedDone: {name}’s cover is recorded: loads that ask for cover are open to them.
tower.courierCover.refusedDone: {name}’s policy was refused; they are shown why.
tower.carrierPapers.coverHint: Read off the policy the fleet sent. While it runs, loads whose sender asks for cover are open to this fleet, and its notes name the cover.
tower.carrierPapers.readFromPhoto: The document this date was read from
tower.carrierPapers.lastRefused: Their last document was not accepted: “{reason}” — {who}, {date}.
tower.carrierPapers.nothingSent: Nothing sent. The fleet sends a renewed document from its dashboard, and it lands here to be read.
tower.carrierPapers.withoutDocument: Record a date without a document
tower.carrierPapers.noProof: This date will rest on no document. Record one this way only if you have the paper itself in front of you — emptying the date clears it.
tower.admins.title: Who can sign in for {name}
tower.admins.name: Their name
tower.admins.nameHint: Recorded against every change they make. Use the name a colleague would recognise.
tower.admins.fold.some: {n, plural, one {# person} other {# people}} can sign in
tower.admins.emptyBody: Until somebody here has a login, only network staff can change what this company charges — which makes its own prices somebody else’s decision.
tower.admins.revealBody: This is the only time it is shown. Hand it over in person or by a channel you trust, and have them change it. Nothing here can show it again — the server keeps only a hash of it.
tower.claims.title: Damage claims
tower.claims.lede: A claim waits here only where the company that carried the parcel has stated cover, and so pays from its own books. Oldest first. Everywhere else a reported problem ends in a damage claim report, listed below.
tower.claims.caveatLead: Every ending carries a reason, including a rejection.
tower.claims.caveat: The claimant is shown what you write. A person whose goods arrived broken is owed an explanation even when they are not owed money.
tower.claims.emptyBody: Nobody is waiting on a decision.
tower.claims.evidenceTitle: What the claimant photographed — {n} attached. Tap one to see it full size.
tower.claims.evidenceOpen: Open the full photograph in a new tab
tower.claims.evidenceNone: No photographs were attached to this claim. That is not a reason to refuse it on its own — but it is a reason to say in your note what you decided on instead.
tower.claims.evidenceMissing: {n} of the {of} attached cannot be opened — the reference is on the record but the photograph is not. Say so in your note if you decide without it.
tower.claims.evidenceGoneTitle: This photograph cannot be opened — the claim cites it, but the file is not there
tower.claims.decided: Decided — {parcel}. The claimant is shown your reason.
tower.claims.shippingSoldFor: Shipping sold for {amount} — not a cap
tower.claims.priceNotRecorded: No shipping price recorded against this parcel
tower.claims.carrierBears: The carrier bears an award up to {amount} — what they were paid for the haul
tower.claims.noCover: NO COVER stated by the company that carried it — nothing can be awarded
tower.claims.noAwardWithoutCover: Nothing can be awarded: the company that carried this parcel has stated no cover, and pays nothing from its own books. Close it as not upheld, with the reason, and point the claimant to the damage claim report.
tower.reports.byShop: By the shop, at its counter
tower.reports.byReceiver: By the receiver, from their app
tower.reports.handedOver: Already handed over to the receiver
tower.reports.downloadFailed: The report could not be downloaded.
tower.claims.decideBody: An award up to {max} can be paid here. Above that it has to be settled off-platform — which is a conversation, not a bigger number in this box.
tower.claims.awardHint: Leave it empty if you are rejecting — a rejection pays nothing by definition.
tower.claims.reasonHint: Shown to the claimant. Write it for them, not for us.
tower.claims.needReason: Every decision needs a reason — including a rejection. The claimant is shown it.
tower.claims.needAward: Upholding a claim means awarding something. Reject it instead of awarding nothing.
tower.claims.overCover: This shipment is covered to {max}. Award up to that, or settle the excess off-platform.
tower.claims.freightAttempts: {n, plural, one {# failed attempt} other {# failed attempts}} before delivery
tower.claims.freightNoBooks: NOTHING BILLED through the network — carriage was settled between sender and carrier. Uphold or reject with a reason; no award is possible here.
tower.claims.freightCovered: Carriage of {amount} billed by us — the company that billed it states cover up to {cover}
tower.claims.freightBilled: Carriage of {amount} billed by us, but the company that billed it has stated NO cover — nothing can be awarded; the note is the report
tower.claims.freightNoAward: Nobody was billed for this load through the network, so there is nothing to award from. Uphold it with a reason that says the money is between sender and carrier, or reject it.
tower.claims.freightDecideBodyNoBooks: The network billed nothing for this load, so no money can be awarded here. Upholding records that the sender was right and that the carriage is theirs and the carrier’s to settle; the sender is shown your reason either way.
tower.disposal.title: Awaiting disposal
tower.disposal.lede: Parcels the receiver gave up and the sender is not paying to recover. Oldest first: each one is a real box in a real shop, in a slot that shop cannot use.
tower.disposal.caveatLead: What happens to them is local law, not a setting.
tower.disposal.caveat: This network does not model a disposal rule it does not know. It shows you the list and what closing one costs, and you apply the rule your jurisdiction actually has.
tower.disposal.emptyBody: No shelf is holding goods nobody wants.
tower.disposal.closeBody: This pays the shop {amount} for the slot it has been holding and hands the slot back. The network absorbs that — nobody else is going to, and a shortfall settling quietly on a shopkeeper who did the work is the one thing this network refuses everywhere else.
tower.disposal.reasonPlaceholder: e.g. Sold at auction under the unclaimed-goods rule, 60 days elapsed
tower.disposal.reasonHint: Kept forever. Somebody may have to answer for this parcel years from now.
tower.disposal.needReason: Say which rule you are applying.
tower.disposal.closed: Closed {parcel} — paid the shop {amount} for the slot it held.
tower.approvals.title: Joining the network
tower.approvals.lede: Shops, drivers and hubs waiting to be let onto the network, and fleets being set up. Until somebody decides, a shopkeeper who signed up is sitting there unable to start.
tower.approvals.emptyBody: No shop is waiting to be let in.
tower.fleets.title: Fleets
tower.fleets.count: On the network: {n} · waiting on you: {waiting}
tower.fleets.lede: A fleet signs itself up on the front page with its four papers, and one of us looks at them. Or register one here: put its papers on record, and a colleague looks at them. Either way, record its bond to make it active — its people then sign in with their own phone number and PIN.
tower.fleets.none: No fleet has been registered yet.
tower.fleets.newHint: The company, its depot, who owns it and its three numbers
tower.fleets.noCountry: No country is switched on yet, so a fleet cannot be registered. Switch one on under Presence first.
tower.fleets.newPhoneHint: The phone number is the one the fleet’s first manager signs in with: a code is texted to it and they choose their own PIN, so it has to be a phone they hold. The owner’s name and ID number go to the identity vault and are not shown again.
tower.fleets.registered: {name} is registered. Next: put its papers on record.
tower.fleets.step.theirs: Sent back — the fleet sends them again
tower.fleets.theirsHint: This fleet signed itself up, so it sends its papers again itself, from the front page. It was emailed the reason above.
tower.fleets.papersHint: A photograph or scan of each of the four. Whoever puts them on record is not the one who approves them: a colleague looks next.
tower.fleets.papersOnRecord: The papers are on record. A colleague looks at them next.
tower.fleets.uploadFailed: A picture could not be uploaded. Choose it again.
tower.fleets.onRecord: Its papers — the certificate of registration, the operator’s licence, the owner’s ID, then the proof of address. Tap one to see it full size.
tower.fleets.sentByFleet: Sent by the fleet itself on {date}. Nobody here entered them, so any one of us may approve them.
tower.fleets.notYours: That was you, so a different member of staff approves them.
tower.fleets.approved: The fleet is approved. Next: record its bond.
tower.fleets.sentBackDone: Sent back. Its papers can be put on record again.
tower.fleets.bondHint: When the fleet’s operating bond has been received, record it here. That makes the fleet active and gives it its code.
tower.fleets.bondRecorded: The fleet is active. Give its office the code shown on its row.
tower.fleets.codeHint: give this to the fleet’s office. In the Fleet app they enter it and tap “Forgot your PIN?”: a code is texted to the phone number above, they add a recovery email, and they choose their own PIN.
tower.reports.notes: {count, plural, one {# note} other {# notes}} the receiver added after handover.
tower.drivers.title: Driver applications
tower.drivers.lede: Heavy-registry drivers waiting on us — new couriers, and drivers in no fleet asking to ride for themselves. What is being judged is whether this person may legally drive, so the licence they sent is shown on the row rather than behind a tap.
tower.drivers.asks: In no fleet, asks to ride for themselves: {vehicle} {plate}, living in {country}. Approving makes them a courier with it; the record check is yours to tick.
tower.drivers.askApproved: Approved — they ride for themselves now, with their own vehicle. They are told on their phone.
tower.drivers.askRefused: Refused — they are shown your reason, stay in no fleet, and may ask again.
tower.drivers.none: No driver is waiting to be vetted.
tower.drivers.recordCleared: I have cleared the criminal-record check
tower.drivers.whatTheySent: What they sent — the licence first, then the ID. Tap one to see it full size.
tower.drivers.nothingToSee: No document images are stored for this driver, so there is nothing here to check. Approving means approving on the typed licence number and expiry alone — say so in your note if you do.
tower.drivers.whyLabel: Why are you refusing these papers?
tower.drivers.approved: Driver approved — their badge is issued.
tower.drivers.refused: Refused — the driver is shown your reason and can send fresh papers.
tower.hubs.title: Hub applications
tower.hubs.lede: Hubs that signed themselves up and sent their papers. Until one is approved it sorts nothing and nothing is routed to it. What is judged is whether this is a real place, licensed to trade, run by the person on the ID — so the papers are on the row.
tower.hubs.none: No hub is waiting to be vetted.
tower.hubs.whatTheySent: What they sent — the licence first, then the ID, then the premises. Tap one to see it full size.
tower.hubs.nothingToSee: No images are stored for these papers, so there is nothing here to check.
tower.hubs.whyLabel: Why are you refusing these papers?
tower.hubs.approved: Hub approved — it can take bags in and sort from now on. It is told.
tower.hubs.refused: Refused — the hub is shown your reason and can send fresh papers.
tower.papers.licenceProof: The licence they sent. Check the date on it before typing one.
tower.papers.licenceNoProof: No image of this licence is stored, so the date below cannot be checked against anything. Recording it puts them back on the road on your word alone.
tower.approvals.noLicencePhoto: No photograph of the licence is stored. Refuse, and ask for one: its date cannot be read from nothing.
tower.approvals.licenceUntil: Trading licence valid until, as you read it
tower.approvals.licenceHint: The last day, as written on the licence. The shop is told thirty days before it runs out; fourteen days after, no new parcel can start there until the renewed one is recorded.
tower.approvals.whyLabel: Why are you refusing this application?
tower.approvals.whyHint: The shop is shown this. Say what was wrong and what they should send instead — they cannot fix what they have not been told.
tower.approvals.approved: Approved — they can start taking parcels.
tower.interest.title: Who is waiting for a country we do not reach
tower.interest.hint: Left on the join form by people in countries the network has not switched on. Most waiting first.
tower.interest.promise: Everyone here was promised one thing and nothing else: that we write to them the day they can sign up in their country — again the day it opens, if sign-ups came first — and say which of the two it became. Approving a change below sends that, to everybody still waiting in it.
tower.langs.title: Languages
tower.langs.lede: Every phrase of the apps, in English, in version 1 as written into the apps, and in your country’s version 2. Write your own words where version 1 reads wrong in your country, or keep version 1 as it is. Version 1 is never changed, and every step is kept with who made it and when; the people in your country read your version 2 from the next time their app opens.
tower.langs.pickCountry: Pick the country whose words you review: one you work in.
tower.langs.searchPh: A word in English or in the language, or a phrase’s key
tower.langs.v1None: not written yet — the app says the English
tower.langs.problemEmpty: Write the words, or keep version 1 as it is.
tower.langs.problemPlaceholders: Keep every one of these exactly, as the English has them: {list}. Without them the screen shows a gap.
tower.docs.title: Terms and notices
tower.docs.lede: What everybody agrees to when they sign up: the terms of use, what happens to their data, and cookies — the general texts, and what a country’s law adds. A change is a new version: one of you writes it with a note saying what changed, and a different one publishes it. Everybody it concerns is told in their app. Every version is kept, and can be read and compared.
tower.docs.generalLede: The general texts: everybody who signs up agrees to these, in every country.
tower.docs.countriesLede: What a country’s law adds, on top of the general texts — never instead of them. Everybody in that country agrees to both: a country’s first version asks all of them, and later ones as you mark them.
tower.docs.exists: {country} has this document already: write its next version in its own panel above.
tower.docs.firstVersion: A first version: there is nothing before it to compare with.
tower.docs.firstAsks: Everybody in {country} is asked to agree to a first version, the next time they open their app.
tower.docs.tellsAll: Once published, everybody with an account is told in their app, with the note above.
tower.docs.tellsCountry: Once published, everybody in {country} is told in their app, with the note above.
tower.docs.held: This names {company}, which is not switched on yet. It is published by the approval that switches it on, under Countries: then everybody in {country} is told {company} is the company they work with, and asked to agree.
tower.docs.fromRecord: Started from {company}’s record: who people in {country} agree with. Add what {country}’s law asks for, and have it read.
